ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.98 to the rider via Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted 18:53–19:01 off-route segment; no account flag.

segment_findings.reason: The only rider-side record is an empty chat [F7]: no rider message before 18:53:40 names any road, area or route, so there is no RD-5 consent to the driver's reroute. The driver's own post-trip statement that he 'took another way' [F8] is a claim, not rider consent (G11). RD-3 is not triggered — no rider-requested stop exists in this segment and no waiting time was billed [F6]. The segment is therefore not excused under RD-3 or RD-5 and is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4(a) is not satisfied by the 18:27 vehicle breakdown [F11]: the off-route segment did not begin until 18:53 [F3], so the incident does not cover the substituted optimal-route stretch the driver actually left.
Band 4 (30–39 km/h) records on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F9][F10] are not the band 1–2 severe congestion of RD-4(b) and, as corroboration only, cannot exempt the segment [RD-4].

An empty chat [F7] cannot supply rider consent, and the driver's post-trip statement that road conditions justified the reroute [F8] is a claim, not the rider's message before the segment that RD-5 requires (G11).
The refund does not fall to $0.00: the sole segment [F3] is not exempt under RD-4 or RD-5, so 2.11 km × $1.41/km = $2.98 is refundable [F6][RD-2].
Accepted only as to quantum mechanics: the 0.29 km residue beyond the 2.11 km segment [F1][F3][F4] is indeed not refundable under RD-2 — but that does not make the segment itself free.
